   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Thurstan Felstead,
                 SOUTH RUISLIP




Dear Brian and Ron,


I just thought it about time I
wrote to you again.


Firstly, I am pleased to see you
thought my humble contributions
were good enough to publish.I've
a few more routines and programs
in the pipeline which should be
with you shortly (other work
permitting).

I am most impressed with your
treatment of contributers. The
payments and free issue of
Outlet are most generous. I have
contributed to YOUR SINCLAIR in
the past and they treat us
contributers terribly. You're
lucky if they leave your code
intact,include the documentation
you sent and spell your name
right. If you want payment for
your efforts or even just a
measly badge then forget it!
They don't even send you a
notification letter! Now that
David McCandless is gone from
Program Pitstop it has improved
a bit but my advice to all
would-be contributers is FORGET
IT! - send your work to Outlet
instead.

I recently attended the 5th All-
Formats show and was impressed
by the variety and diversity of
the items on display, even if
attendance wasn't quite up to
scratch. I hadn't been to a
computer show since the '88 ZX
Microfair and was finally pers-
aded to attend when SAMCO sent
me a free ticket with their
information pack.

I arrived late (about 1.30pm)
and went straight to the SAMCo
stand in the hope of obtaining a
SAM Coupe ROM/DOS upgrade.
Unfortunately, I was informed by
the ever-pleasant Alan Miles
that the fifty packs they had
brought to the show with them
were gone by 11am.

I put in an order with him; also
purchased four MGT disk boxes
for 50p each and SAM "Defenders
of the Earth" on disk for `12.

Apparently version 3.0 of the
SAM Coupe ROM is now available
but I'm not sure whether it will
be shipped in the currently
advertised pack, superceding
2.0. It is good to see that
SAMCo do not intend to make the
mistakes that MGT did, they are
charging for the upgrade and
have put the Coupe Hotline on an
0898 number.

Enigma Variations, producers of
SAM Defenders of the Earth, were
on the SAMCo stand with impress-
ive demos of some up-and-coming
games.

They were also promoting a SAM
Software Club. This club, which
costs `10 per annum to join, is
dedicated to bringing SAM Coupe
software (and hardware) to users
at reasonable prices. They are
currently offering pounds off
the latest SAM software and will
continue to do so. Write to
Enigma Variations Ltd., 13 North
Park Road, Harrogate, HG1 5PD
(tel: 0423 501595) for more
details.

Next to the SAMCo stand was Blue
Alpha Electronics with what is
probably the first SAM Coupe
third party add-on, the Voicebox
speech synthesiser. This compact
unit,which fits onto the Coupe's
expansion port,is phoneme-based.

It comes with driver software
that allows written English to
be converted into speech. It
costs `29.99 and is available
from Blue Alpha Electronics,
Ynysforgan Farm, Morriston,
Swansea,SA6 6QL(tel:0792 310865)

Another honorable mention goes
to the Spectrum Discovery Club's
SAM Supplement: a disk magazine
premiered at the show. It's
similar in style to Outlet (but
not quite as professional) with
the same mix of letters,
routines, demos and games. The
spelling and punctuation leaves
a lot to be desired but the
content is credible and varied,
with the overall feel good.

Programs in issue one include
three impressive graphics demos,
extra sound effects from BASIC
and a program to test the speed
of your drives! The editor is
David Tonks and members/ contri-
buters include Dr. Andy Wright
(who wrote SAM BASIC), Dr. John
Wase(who wrote for Popular Comp-
uting Weekly) and Simon Goodwin
(of Crash Tech Niche fame). My
opinion is that the Supplement
is definitely worth getting.

Write to Brian Mumford, 57 St.
Saviours Road, West Croydon,
Surrey CR0 2XE (tel: 081-689
1439) enclosing `1.50 to obtain
the latest issue on 3.5" disk or
enclose your own blank,formatted
disk and return postage(cheques/
P.O.s payable to SDC).

If you've seen machines like the
Apple Macintosh or Atari ST, you
will know how wonderful their
Graphical User Interfaces are.
You may have sat at your humble
Spectrum afterwards and thought,
"wouldn't it be wonderful if my
Speccy could have an operating
system like that?". Well now,
thanks to those nice people at
Garner Designs, your Spectrum +3
can!Their package,Desktop Execu-
tive, gives your +3 a true front
end WIMP (Windows, Icons, Menus
and Pointers)-driven operating
system to replace the clumsy +3
DOS one. Included in the package
are a WIMP-driven Diary, Machine
Code Disassembler and Character
Set Designer. A facility to use
the WIMP system in your own pro-
grams is also included.

At `16.95 it may seem a bit
pricey, but think of all the fun
you can have pretending your
`200 Spectrum is a `2000 Mac!
Daniel Garner, the proprietor of
Garner Designs, also runs the
Plus Three Users Group. Write to
the same address for details.
Garner Designs Software, 57
Lovers Walk, Dunstable, Beds.,
LU5 4BG (tel: 0582 472067).

In a surprise move, Century have
ceased publication of "Hacker's
Handbook". After six years they
were apparently forced to stop
production by the new Computer
Misuse Bill coming in this year.
This is a real shame as the book
has been a consistently-invalu-
able reference work on Comms
over the years.

Only a few hundred copies of the
latest edition (IV) are still
available on shop shelves so if
you want a copy you'd better act
quickly.           T.F.

Many thanks, Thurstan. Yes, we
should, perhaps remind readers
more often that we do PAY for
any contributions published.This
ranges from `3 to `5 for a very
short review or routine to `20
UPWARDS for mega-programs but
typical programs attract `8 to
`12. Incidentally, free issues
are not normally added although
some readers prefer payments to
be credited to their OUTLET sub-
scription. Contributions MUST be
your own work, public domain or
have permission from the author.
                           B.C.

From: Ian Kennedy, EXETER

I am home on leave from Botswana
where I bought my first Spectrum
about six years ago. It seems
impossible I could have gone all
that time without knowing about
OUTLET but now having found you
I have to say that you seem to
be one of the most user-friendly
groups around.I am amazed at the
high quality of the "show" and
the effort that must go into it.

I started life with an Opus
Drive but that soon died on me
and I converted to Disciple
which works well. I have since
come into contact with the
Spectrum Discovery Club who put
me onto a repairer for my Opus.

So, my first question is: If I
get OUTLET on a Disciple disk,
can I use the Opus programs or
do I have to have a disk for
each version? Similarly with
SAM/Speccy disks? My printer is
a Brother M1009.

Arriving so late on the scene I
can't afford all the back num-
bers I'd like but one suggestion
I have is to put all Tasword
programs on an EXTRA disc as
these are the ones I would find
most useful.

Where can I get an SSTT (slow
scan TV converter)?I got a video
digitiser through MGT but could
never get it to work.

Can you do a series on the make-
up of the different file types?
I have four books on microdrives
but still haven't a clue what a
PRINT file is and why I get the
message "wrong file type".Why is
it wrong and what can I do about
it? This is a special problem in
trying to deal with Tasword 2
and 3 textfiles on microdrive.

Is there a quick way of discov-
ering the code address and
length of Tasword files so that
they can be saved to tape and
reloaded to disc?

Why is it so difficult to load
T2 files into T3 for use of T3's
wider selection of functions?

                   Ian Kennedy

To Ian Kennedy from Brian Gaff



Well, quite a varied selection
of questions there Ian!

Firstly,you should have no prob-
lems running the Opus prorams
although you will have to load
them in from your Disciple
system and then save them to
tape. In most Outlet programs,
you will find a tape SAVE placed
around line 9983.

It should then be just a case of
loading the programs back into
your Opus system, and saving
them to disc.

Sadly, you cannot do this with
the SAM version of Outlet. Even
programs with the same names as
those on the Spectrum version
have been irreversibly converted
into SAM BASIC, sorry.

Most of the Tasword additions we
have published are for Tasword
2, and I am not sure if there
would be a market for a disc
full of modifications for it.

The main difference between
Tasword 2 and the other Taswords
are the way the file itself is
constructed. Tasword 2 stores
text as a continuous string of
printable characters. So, if you
set your right margin to 32,
there will be 32 characters of

the first line, followed by 32
spaces, which in turn will be
followed by the 32 characters of
line 2, etc.

This method is very wasteful or
RAM, so later versions used a
simpler method. They attach a
CHR$ 13 and a CHR$ 10 to the end
of each line, and don't bother
with the trailing spaces. Thus,
even if you convert Tasword 3
PRINT files into CODE ones, you
end up with rather a mess when
you load it into Tasword 2!

Tasman normally provide a con-
version program to let you load
Tasword 2 files into Tasword 3,
at least I had one on my Micro-
drive version.

Filetypes like CODE and BASIC
are described by the header they
use. PRINT files have no header
and must be read from a stream.

Try this on a Tasword 3 file:

10 OPEN #4;"m";1;"file"
20 MOVE #4 TO #2

On Microdrive, this will read
the PRINT file called "file" and
shove it to stream 2, which is
the screen.

The ROMBO Digitizer works very
well, it should need no more
than a signal from a video - NOT
the aerial. In other words, if
your video has no video output,
then you are stuck!

Slow scan TV is rather a
specialist subject. I have come
accross a Belgian program which
gives SSTV, RTTY and Morse
decoding without any other
interface being needed. It is
fair to say though that I have
had little luck getting the SSTV
part to work! The main problem
is that the Spectrum generates
so much RF interference, it
almost blots out the signals.

Your best bet is to write to the
RSGB, as they will probably have
details of any Spectrum Ham
Radio User Groups that may
exist.
                          B.G.

Mr. John Couch 3, Burnham Drive,
Newton, Swansea, SA3 4TW

Thank you for the first 4 copies
of OUTLET and OUTLET EXTRA. I'm
sure many Speccy owners would
love to receive it but don't
know about it. Could you not
advertise in SU, YS and CRASH?

When pressing "W"in JOTTER I get
"NONSENSE IN BASIC 8160:2".

Keep up the good work. I am a
65-year-old,absolute novice with
a 128K+2a.
           John Couch

Please print my full address in
case anyone inn (Freudian slip!)
my neck of the woods would like
to get in contact.

To John Couch from Brian Cavers

Thanks John.

We DO already advertise every
month in SINCLAIR USER but our
extremely meagre resources limit
us to a tiny "classified" block.
We do have small-ads in several
of the other magazines as well
and modestly-larger adverts in
NEW COMPUTER EXPRESS and FORMAT.

The error message in JOTTER may
be ignored. If you wish to stop
it just remove the # after CLS #
in line 8160. Incidentally, when
writing in JOTTER,you should use
DATA statements - NOT PRINT!

                            B.C.

From: D.A.Turton, LIVERPOOL

As you may have noticed from my
last letter to you, I have
purchased a new printer. It is
the PANASONIC KX-P1081 Printer,
and I am still trying to get
used to it.

The software program I am using
with it at the moment is Tasword
with Tas-Print, I think you will
agree the printing is not bad at
all.

Perhaps you could help me with
one small problem, that is, I
don't know how to print the
pound symbol, all I seem able to
print is ( # )perhaps you have
the answer?

Also, when using Tas-Print, the
configuration part at the
beginning gives a list of print-
ers with which the program will
work. Panasonic is mentioned but
a different model to mine, i.e.,
KX-P1091. Would this make any
difference to my model?

           D.A.TURTON

This is a common problem and you
will find a detailed solution in
my reply to Mr. C.M. Howell in
last month's OUTLET.In your case
you might consider just changing
the dipswitch in your printer
(see your printer manual) to the
English character set and use
the # symbol instead of a `.This
will then print out as a `.
                           B.C.

From: Leslie Quinn,SCOTLAND

Does anyone have a piece of code
to calculate the screen address
to print an 8x8 pixel character
on-screen 10-192 pixel(x co-ord)
to stop the screen 'thirds' from
breaking up the character?


If you load the B register with
a character line number (24= top
line down to 1= bottom line) and
CALL 3739 (#0E9B), the first
screen address of that line is
returned in HL. Just increment
by 256 for each pixel line below
and add 1 for each character
square along the line(This is on
a Spectrum I hasten to add!).
                           B.C.

From:Fred Nostdal, SOUTH SHIELDS

Dear Ron,
Many thanks for your kind and

set my mind at rest when I read

ation and stating that he had

had received the books with no
bother.

I have mentioned before that I
have written up and down the
length of the country each time
enclosing S.A.E.'s and so far
without success. The above
failure is just another to add
to my list.
            I remain,

        Yours faithfully,

          Fred Nostdal

Brian Cavers to Fred Nostdal

Your letter or their reply may
have gone astray in the post.Are
you certain you made no error in
the address?Was it legible? Even
if correctly addressed there is
a chance it was misdirected. I
usually try twice THEN get more
insistent on the third try and
only blow my top on the fourth
attempt!

If you have this sort of trouble
more frequently than Mr. Average
you are either very unlucky or
possibly making errors somehow.
It's surprising how many forget
to include THEIR OWN address or
write it illegibly or incorrect-
ly. Who are you anyway?
                           B.C..

From Harold Burton, EDINBURGH

Dear Ron and Brian,

Thank you for another disk of
superb programs. Every month is
a winner!

Regarding the correspondence on
printing out from MASTERFILE, I
would like to refer you to my
solution in FORMAT Vol. 3 No.3
page 8 which I find works very
well. I will repeat the details
below.

Amend the BASIC as follows:

4010 POKE @6,1: INPUT;: COPY
SCREEN$: LPRINT CHR$ 27; CHR$
106; CHR$ 51;: INPUT;: POKE @6,0
: GOTO TO USR r

4900 POKE @6,1: LPRINT CHR$ 27;
CHR$ 64; CHR$ 27; CHR$ 108; CHR$
15; CHR$ 27; CHR$ 67; CHR$ 0;
CHR$ 11; CHR$ 27; CHR$ 78; CHR$
8;: POKE @6,0: GOTO USR r


Line 4010 causes the print
routine to omit the two bottom
lines of the MF page, then do a
reverse line feed so that there
is no space between printing
pages. "CHR$ 51" can be amended
to suit the size of record.


Line 4900 sets the printer mar-
gin and perforation skip for 11"
paper and is activated by press-
ing "U" and "Y" for USR BASIC.

If one has incorporated a head-
ing at the top of the file page,
this can be omitted by defining
an additional format without
including it then the amount of
reverse linefeed can be increas-
ed to provide a continuous print
out.
      Trust this is useful.

         Yours sincerely

          HAROLD BURTON


Many thanks. However, readers
should note that many printers
cannot do a reverse linefeed so
you may have to put up with the
extra spacing.
                         - B.C.

From Matthew P. Kendall,BRADFORD



Dear Ron & Brian,

LC-10 control codes may,however,

Thank you for a great monthly
read.I particularly liked'Brot'.
How about more fractal programs?

       MATTHEW.P.KENDALL.

Thanks,Matthew. There'll be more
about BROT in next month's issue
of OUTLET.                  B.C.

From Brian Cavers

Ron's now got a new +D and two
new drives as back-up for his
main system and I've now got a
new Disciple and twin drives.

From the very beginning, EVERY
issue and version of OUTLET has
begun life on microdrive then
converted at the end of the
month. The only exceptions are
SAM-specific programs which are
added to replace any Spectrum
programs that won't convert. I
must eventually make the trans-
ition to the Disciple as my main
system but this may take months.
Suffice to say for now,I recomm-
end the Disciple to anyone with
microdrives looking to upgrade.

The reason is,the Disciple works
happily with Interface 1 so you
can use both either indefinitely
or for the changeover period. In
addition, most microdrive pro-
grams work straightaway on the
Disciple - the main exception
being OPEN #3;"T" etc.

Most files can be transferred to
disc by loading from microdrive;
pressing a button and SAVEing to
disc!Press the button again then
RANDOMIZE USR 0 or OUT 31,0 and
you LOAD from microdrive again!
Alternatively, leave the button
in and use OUT 31,16 to switch
to Disciple and OUT 31,0 to use
Interface 1. You could put that
in a program to switch from one
to the other easily!

SAM users may often find a spare
character appears in an INPUT
which has to be deleted before
you can enter your text. The odd
character is the last key used
and appears because one of the
system variables is not properly
updated. To cure the problem put
POKE 23611, PEEK 23611, BAND 128
before the INPUT.

My nephew, Richard Maughan,found
how to pass OCTON in DEFENDERS
OF THE EARTH. You need to shoot
the beast repeatedly. There's no
indication of progress but it
does eventually work.Keep to the
left, crouch then jump and fire
as OCTON shoots a low barrage.
Well done Richard - I'd already
given it up as hopeless.

Finally, here's an infinite life
cheat for the game. If you run
one game and get to the high
score table enter .....ORB as
your name (not ORB.....).

You can then play without losing
shields except if you fall in
water. At later stages there are
unjumpable chasms which must be
crossed by pressing "1" for help
from the other defenders just as
when trying to get through some
of the doors.
                          B.C.

From Paul Oliver

When loading one program from
within another program (e.g. a
"CATLOADER"-type program),if the
program being loaded is not an
auto-run program then the error
report "Nonsense in BASIC" is
returned.Is there any way around
this?(Maybe making the LOAD look

A spent an hour or two on this,

to try? Incidentally, the same
bug is on the SAM -even if KEYIN
is used without a line number.

                         - B.C.

From David Wornham, FLEXIBASE
SOFTWARE, WORCS.

Congratulations on a continuing
all-round excellence with Out-
let.I was particularly impressed
with the Sam animated graphics
of the Dragon and Waterfall.Keep
up the good work.

I will be attending both the
Stafford Alternative Micro Show
and Radio Rally at the Bingley
Hall, Stafford Show Ground 10am
to 5pm, Saturday, 10th November
and the 8-Bit Micro Show show at
Tamworth Arts Centre on Saturday
1st December with Flexipage
Sales and demonstrations on
Spectrum and Sam Coupe and
would be grateful for a mention.

In case you and your members
have not spotted them, I have
found the following differences
from Spectrum in the new Sam
ROM, but cannot say if they were
present in the old Sam ROM:

FOR A=A TO 10 is not accepted.
First LET A=1 etc.

After DIM a$(10,10) etc, PRINT
A$(a)(b) is not accepted, but
PRINT A$(a,b) is.


Thanks David, although I think
there is a misprint in your
letter because PRINT A$(a) (b)
is meaningless on both SAM and
Spectrum.
                          B.C.

The main difference between Tasword 2 and the other Taswords are the way the file itself is constructed. Tasword 2 stores text as a continuous string of printable characters. So, if you set your right margin to 32, there will be 32 characters of

the first line, followed by 32 spaces, which in turn will be followed by the 32 characters of line 2, etc.

This method is very wasteful or RAM, so later versions used a simpler method. They attach a CHR$ 13 and a CHR$ 10 to the end of each line, and don't bother with the trailing spaces. 10 OPEN #4;"m";1;"file" 20 MOVE #4 TO #2

Основное различие между Tasword 2 и другими версиями Tasword заключается в способе построения самого файла. Tasword 2 хранит текст как непрерывную строку печатаемых символов. Поэтому, если вы установите правое поле на 32, будет 32 символа первой строки, за которыми последуют 32 пробела, а затем 32 символа второй строки и так далее.

Этот метод очень расточителен по отношению к оперативной памяти, поэтому в более поздних версиях использовался более простой способ. Они добавляют CHR$ 13 и CHR$ 10 в конец каждой строки и не утруждают себя лишними пробелами. Таким образом, даже если вы сконвертируете файлы PRINT из Tasword 3 в файлы CODE, при загрузке в Tasword 2 получится полный беспорядок!

Tasman обычно предоставляет программу конвертации, позволяющую загружать файлы Tasword 2 в Tasword 3; по крайней мере, она была у меня на версии для Microdrive.

Типы файлов, такие как CODE и BASIC, описываются заголовком, который они используют. Файлы PRINT не имеют заголовка и должны считываться из потока.

Попробуйте это на файле Tasword 3:

```text
10 OPEN #4;"m";1;"file"
20 MOVE #4 TO #2
```

На микродрайве это прочитает файл PRINT с именем «file» и отправит его в поток 2, который является экраном.

### От: Brian Cavers

У Рона теперь есть новый +D и два новых дисковода в качестве резерва для его основной системы, а у меня теперь новый Disciple и сдвоенный дисковод.

С самого начала КАЖДЫЙ номер и версия OUTLET зарождались на микродрайве, а в конце месяца конвертировались. Единственным исключением являются специальные программы для SAM, которые добавляются взамен тех спектрумовских программ, которые не удается сконвертировать. Рано или поздно мне придется перейти на Disciple в качестве основной системы, но это может занять месяцы. Пока же скажу кратко: я рекомендую Disciple всем владельцам микродрайвов, желающим проапгрейдиться.

Причина в том, что Disciple прекрасно работает в паре с Interface 1, так что вы можете использовать их оба либо постоянно, либо на время переходного периода. Кроме того, большинство программ для микродрайва сразу работают на Disciple — главным исключением является OPEN #3;"T" и т. д.

Большинство файлов можно перенести на диск, загрузив их с микродрайва, нажав кнопку и сделав SAVE на диск! Нажмите кнопку снова, затем RANDOMIZE USR 0 или OUT 31,0 — и вы снова можете делать LOAD с микродрайва! Либо оставьте кнопку нажатой и используйте OUT 31,16 для переключения на Disciple и OUT 31,0 для использования Interface 1. Это можно вставить в программу, чтобы легко переключаться с одного на другой!

Пользователи SAM часто могут заметить, что при выполнении INPUT появляется лишний символ, который приходится стирать перед вводом текста. Этот лишний символ — последняя нажатая клавиша, и появляется он из-за того, что одна из системных переменных не обновляется должным образом. Чтобы устранить проблему, поместите перед INPUT строку:
`POKE 23611, PEEK 23611, BAND 128`

Мой племянник, Richard Maughan, нашел способ пройти OCTON в DEFENDERS OF THE EARTH. Нужно стрелять по этой твари непрерывно. Никаких признаков урона нет, но в итоге это срабатывает. Держитесь левой стороны, приседайте, затем подпрыгивайте и стреляйте, когда OCTON дает низкий залп. Молодец, Richard — я уже махнул рукой и считал это место непроходимым.

И напоследок — чит на бесконечные жизни для этой игры. Если вы сыграете одну игру и дойдете до таблицы рекордов, введите в качестве имени `.....ORB` (не `ORB.....`).

После этого вы сможете играть, не теряя щиты, за исключением случаев падения в воду. На более поздних этапах встречаются непроходимые пропасти, которые нужно пересекать, нажимая «1» для вызова помощи других защитников — точно так же, как при попытке пройти через некоторые двери.
